summary: Monolith ASP.NET Core on .NET 10 LTS on Azure App Service with Azure SQL Database as the database in India; front end: Blazor.

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable ASP.NET Core on .NET 10 LTS app: 2 engineer(s) and scale level L2 do not justify splitting services. Microservices rejected: 2 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Lets a C# team build the UI without switching to JavaScript. Fit for this project: team.languages includes C#; well suited to internal tool projects; C# is listed first (treated as the team's primary language); strong maintainability, which you rated 5/5.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes C#).

tradeoffs: Smaller UI component ecosystem than React.
WebAssembly mode has a heavy first load; Server mode needs a live connection.

backend.justification: High-performance C# on .NET 10 LTS (supported to Nov 2028; .NET 8 support ended 10 Nov 2026) with first-class Entra ID and SignalR support. Fit for this project: team.languages includes C#; first-class Microsoft Entra ID integration; strong maintainability, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (first-class Microsoft Entra ID integration).
Excluded: AWS is not on Azure, and cloud_preference=azure is a hard constraint (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Best tooling assumes the Microsoft ecosystem.

database.justification: Reuses existing SQL Server skills, schemas and tooling. Fit for this project: reuses the existing SQL Server / Azure SQL Database data and skills; strong security, which you rated 4/5; strong maintainability, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 5/5. Data stays in Central India (Pune) to satisfy data_residency=india.

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server (Central India (Pune))
alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (reuses the existing SQL Server / Azure SQL Database data and skills).

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server (Central India (Pune))
alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (reuses the existing SQL Server / Azure SQL Database data and skills).
Excluded: Google Cloud is not on Azure, and cloud_preference=azure is a hard constraint (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Licensing makes self-hosted or non-Azure deployments expensive.

hosting.justification: Managed web hosting with built-in Entra ID sign-in, slots and VNet integration. Fit for this project: strong time to market, which you rated 5/5; well suited to internal tool projects; built-in Entra ID sign-in (Easy Auth).

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: no india region (fine for public static files, but keeps the app outside the residency zone).
Lower overall fit: some infrastructure to operate with no DevOps engineer; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).
Excluded: AWS is not on Azure, and cloud_preference=azure is a hard constraint (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Per-instance pricing does not scale to zero.

supporting.justification: The organisation's directory is Microsoft (listed in existing_systems), so the app trusts Entra ID via OpenID Connect: no new passwords, and joiners/leavers are handled centrally. App Service 'Easy Auth' can enforce sign-in with no auth code.

alternatives.why_not: Would duplicate the identity provider the company already runs.

tradeoffs: Sign-in depends on the corporate IdP's availability; keep a break-glass admin account.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with short-lived SAS tokens, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: Fine for documents, poor as app storage.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (image/file processing, approval e-mails) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Listed in existing_systems; integrate through its official API with a service account and least-privilege scopes rather than duplicating its data.

supporting.choice: Migration and integration plan for existing systems
supporting.justification: On-prem SQL Server 2019: same engine as the recommended database, so lift the schema and data with Azure Database Migration Service and upgrade to a supported version in the same step.

alternatives.why_not: Higher risk: everything switches at once with no fallback.

tradeoffs: Running old and new systems in parallel costs extra for a few weeks.

supporting.choice: Azure Key Vault + Activity Log + Azure WAF
supporting.justification: Compliance controls for ISO27001: encryption keys you control, no secrets in code, tamper-evident audit logs and a web application firewall.

alternatives.why_not: Auditors expect platform-level key management and logs.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + OpenTelemetry tracing
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data; Sentry has no India data region.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L2: ~1500 users, ~300 peak concurrent, ~60 req/s at peak, ~20 GB stored
Upper bound capped at ~3x the lower bound: components do not all reach their peak tier in the same month
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: Existing system 'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)': Azure AD is now Microsoft Entra ID; same service, new name. Integrate via OIDC/SAML. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/new-name

Existing system 'On-prem SQL Server 2019': Mainstream support ended 28 Feb 2025; extended (security-only) support runs to 8 Jan 2030. Plan an upgrade or migrate to Azure SQL Database. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/sql-server-2019
The low estimate ($102) fits the $300 budget, but the upper estimate ($356) exceeds it as usage grows; set billing alerts and use the cost-control notes in each component.

CERT-In Directions (28 Apr 2022): keep system logs for 180 days within India and report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours; size log retention and the incident runbook accordingly. Source: https://www.cert-in.org.in/Directions70B.jsp

An existing SQL Server is listed: migrate the relevant tables to the managed database (Azure Database Migration Service / DMS) or reach the on-prem server through a private connection; do not expose it publicly.
